archetype: WU forced-draw punisher control with a hug-fort shell: symmetric table-draw engines feeding asymmetric hand-size punishers, a Displacer Kitten blink engine converting spell velocity into permanent re-use, and Heliod, the Warped Eclipse converting opponents' draws into cost reduction and flash-speed control

role_assignment.default_role: control with inevitability: the punisher upkeep damage (verified in stack 003: Iron Maiden + Ebony Owl Netsuke deal 7 on the punished upkeep once Forced Fruition has filled the hand, and cleanup trims to exactly 7) is a clock that runs without tapping out; the counterspell suite (free/cheap interaction held in 73.3% of goldfish games) plus Supreme Verdict — the uncounterable creature reset the previous build lacked — defend the long game. Whoever loses the long game must be the beatdown, and here that is usually not you (strategy:whos-the-beatdown, strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). The new hug-fort layer (Kwain, The Second Doctor) buys the waiting turns politically: the table draws with you, and Second Doctor's rider deters the players who accept (strategy:multiplayer.politics)
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: either (a) the core two-piece (table engine + punisher) is assembled and Heliod's discount is live — goldfish says by turn 6 in only 39.6% of games, improved from 34.3% by the two new engine pieces but still not automatic — or (b) Approach of the Second Sun with the second cast set up (verified stack 002) and the table's open mana counted; commit only when the attempt can't be profitably answered, holding Dovin's Veto/Swan Song for the commit turn, not after (strategy:pivot-point, strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window)

engines.piece: Forced Fruition + Iron Maiden + Ebony Owl Netsuke
engines.engine: the punisher core: force draws (Forced Fruition, Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Temple Bell, Dictate of Kruphix, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Folio of Fancies) into hand-size upkeep damage (Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke, Viseling) — a two-piece critical-mass engine that is inert below threshold and a table-wide clock past it. Opponents still trim to seven at cleanup, which is why the punishers hit on upkeep, before the drawn cards are spent (verified sequencing in stack 003). Deck-facts still flags most of this core as role-untagged — histograms undercount the real plan
engines.evidence: verified stack 003 (7 damage on the punished upkeep incl. the cleanup-trims-to-7 subtlety); oracle text; goldfish target 'Engine + punisher assembled' 39.6% by t6, 54.8% ever

engines.engine: the blink engine, first-class in this build: 'Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, exile up to one target nonland permanent you control, then return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control.' In a list whose 67 nonlands are mostly noncreature spells, every cast is a blink: a blinked Sol Ring returns untapped (mana back per noncreature cast); a blinked Mystic Remora returns as a new object with zero age counters (the cumulative-upkeep tax never compounds — a free Remora for as long as Kitten watches it); a blinked Loran of the Third Path re-triggers 'destroy up to one target artifact or enchantment' and returns untapped for another draw activation, as do Kwain's and Faerie Mastermind's tap/activated uses on their own bodies. This is an engine that scales with the deck's own spell velocity — an inevitability source in Duke's sense. Its one tempting degenerate extension is now REFUTED: stack 005 shows Kitten does NOT make the Hullbreaker loop mana-positive — both triggers lock targets at announcement and the exiled-and-returned permanent is a new object (400.7/608.2b), so Horror's bounce and Kitten's blink are mutually exclusive per cast. The loop stays exactly mana-neutral with unbounded casts; a Kitten-first ordering is a one-time, loop-terminating exit worth +1 float (terminal float 3 vs 2), capping any in-loop X payoff at actual float ≤3
engines.evidence: oracle text (Displacer Kitten, Mystic Remora, Sol Ring, Loran of the Third Path); verified stack 005 (mana-positive claim refuted; +1-float terminal exit verified); the Remora age-counter reset value line remains unverified and is queued below

engines.piece: Kwain, Itinerant Meddler + The Second Doctor + Alhammarret's Archive
engines.engine: the hug-fort layer, new in this build: Kwain taps to let everyone draw (drawers gain 1 life); The Second Doctor offers an end-step draw whose rider — 'Each opponent who does can't attack you or permanents you control during their next turn' — converts generosity into a pillow-fort effect that blanks attack plans from three players, alongside Propaganda and Ghostly Prison; and both hug pieces feed the punisher math, since every card the table accepts pushes hands toward the Iron Maiden / Netsuke thresholds. Alhammarret's Archive is the asymmetry hinge: your Kwain and Mine-effect draws double while opponents' don't, and 'you gain twice that much life instead' doubles Kwain's drip and turns a first Approach of the Second Sun into 14 life. The Second Doctor and Thought Vessel also give YOU no maximum hand size to hoard the doubled draws
engines.evidence: oracle text (Kwain, The Second Doctor, Alhammarret's Archive, Propaganda, Ghostly Prison); goldfish target 'Table draw engine drawn' 72.3% by t6, mean turn 2.6

engines.engine: the hinge that makes the symmetric draw asymmetric: spells cost {1} less per card opponents drew this turn and everything gains flash, so the table-draw engines pay your mana bill and let you hold up counterspells while deploying — the deck's version of making the opponents' cards work for you; the hug pieces (Kwain activations, Second Doctor end-step draws) directly grow the discount on the turns you want to act
engines.evidence: oracle text (back face: flash grant + per-opponent-draw cost reduction); goldfish: commander mean cast turn 4.098, 90.8% by t6

engines.piece: Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring + Arcane Signet
engines.engine: verified unbounded-cast loop: alternating-bounce of the two rocks is exactly mana-neutral per cycle, giving unbounded cast/storm count in one main phase — but it nets no mana, cards, or damage on its own; Thought Vessel substitutes exactly for Arcane Signet, Fellwar Stone is board-conditional. The two-card Hullbreaker + Sol Ring 'infinite' in the combo DB is REFUTED (stack 001): no repeatable sequence exists with only those two cards
engines.evidence: verified stack 004 (engine real, mana-neutral); verified stack 001 (two-card version refuted); the combo_details line for the pair is not fact

engines.piece: Approach of the Second Sun + Mystical Tutor
engines.engine: the clean win line: first Approach resolves and goes seventh from the top (gaining 14 life, not 7, with Alhammarret's Archive out), Mystical Tutor puts it back on top the turn you re-draw it, second cast wins — with the opponents' interaction window on the second cast explicitly walked through and survivable behind held countermagic. With White Sun's Zenith cut, this line carries more of the wincon-access weight
engines.evidence: verified stack 002 (second-cast win incl. the interaction window); goldfish target 'Win condition access' 42.6% by t6, down from the prior build

engines.piece: Rhystic Study / Mystic Remora / Consecrated Sphinx / Teferi's Ageless Insight / Faerie Mastermind / Smothering Tithe
engines.engine: asymmetric value layer riding the same forced-draw turbulence: while the punishers tax opponents' hands, these convert the table's activity into your cards and treasure — and Teferi's Ageless Insight stacks with Alhammarret's Archive as a second your-side draw doubler
engines.evidence: oracle text; goldfish target 'Heliod down with an asymmetric card engine' 54.0% by t6, 70.2% ever

candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Tithe triggers once per opponent draw with a {2} opt-out; Forced Fruition makes every opponent spell 7 draws, so one opponent turn can present 7+ pay-or-treasure decisions — the trigger count, the may-pay timing, and the realistic treasure yield have not been walked through

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: You are rarely the beatdown by label, but in a control mirror someone must be (strategy:whos-the-beatdown) — and your punishers are a clock that advances during draw-go, so you own inevitability (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock) and can let them act first. Creature sweepers hit almost nothing here; the real exposure is artifact/enchantment mass removal taking the engine and punisher layers together — deploy in layers, bank countermagic for the pivot turn (strategy:pivot-point). New this build: Supreme Verdict is YOUR uncounterable reset, so in the mirror you can wrath through their permission at no counterspell cost.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Taxes attack exactly this deck's velocity math — many cheap spells per turn — so recount your hand under the tax (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial). You rarely own the long game under an assembling lock: role flips to beatdown, racing the lock's completion. Heliod's per-opponent-draw discount is a partial tax rebate unique to this deck, and the forced-draw engines keep feeding it even under a lock; Displacer Kitten re-triggering Loran's ETB removal gives repeatable answers to the lock pieces themselves. Layered pieces are the danger — answer the compounding second piece, not the first inconvenience.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: Propaganda, Ghostly Prison, and now The Second Doctor's attack-deterrent rider are virtual card advantage tripled in multiplayer — one pillow-fort effect blanks attack plans from three players (strategy:card-advantage.virtual) — and the punishers convert defense into a clock, pushing the aggressor's damage-per-card below lethal (strategy:life-as-resource.philosophy-of-fire). Supreme Verdict is the uncounterable catch-up button when deterrence fails; per sweeper math, commit little board yourself and let the aggro player overextend into it (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). The trap remains: Forced Fruition refuels the aggro player's hand — sequence punishers before or with the big draw engines so the refill is taxed on arrival (strategy:critical-mass).
matchup_frames.vs_combo: Hold the free suite (Fierce Guardianship, Force of Negation, Swan Song, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Dovin's Veto — held in 73.3% of goldfish games) for the card that ends the game if it resolves, per the answer-economy bar (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy). The deck-specific warning: Forced Fruition hands a combo pilot seven cards per spell, and Kwain/Second Doctor draws are gifts too — against storm or spellslinger pods the hug layer is a liability, not an engine. Your artifact engines read as quiet; expect experienced tables to discount your 'I haven't done anything' and hit you anyway (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection).

distribution_notes: 85 entries / 100 copies with only 18 land entries; curve is aggressively low (9/21/17 at MV 1-3, nine cards at MV 5+) because the deck expects Heliod's discount to pay the top end. Pips skew hard blue: 50 U pips across 35 cards (source target 36) versus 14 W pips across 13 (target 22) — Heliod's front face is W but the operating colour is U. Goldfish after the rebuild: commander mean cast 4.098 (median 4, 90.8% by t6), keep-first-seven 74.2%; the engine half is drawn in 72.3% of games by t6 and the core two-piece assembles by t6 in 39.6% (up from 34.3% — Kwain and The Second Doctor did that), but wincon access fell to 42.6% by t6 with White Sun's Zenith cut: the deck got more consistent at its engine and thinner at closing. It still spends most early games as draw-go control holding interaction (73.3% held). Mulligan accordingly: engine-half hands (a Mine effect) dig toward punishers; punisher-only hands are blanks until the engine exists (strategy:mulligans.engine-hands). 23 cards, including nearly the whole punisher core, carry no role tag — the role histogram materially undercounts the plan. Bracket floor is 4 (Optimized): 8 Game Changers force it independent of the combo story, which matters because stack 001 refuted the DB's two-card infinite that the bracket report also lists as a floor-4 driver.
overall_assessment: This deck plays the long game on purpose and makes the whole table pay for its card advantage. Its world-view is Duke's inevitability (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock): every symmetric draw is asymmetric three ways — it feeds Heliod's cost reduction, the hand-size punishers, and the Tithe/Sphinx value layer — and the rebuild sharpened both halves of that identity. The hug-fort layer (Kwain, The Second Doctor, Alhammarret's Archive) makes the waiting game actively political: the table draws with you, attacking you is disincentivized by rider and by self-interest, and the Archive quietly makes every shared effect pay you double (strategy:multiplayer.politics, strategy:card-advantage.virtual). Displacer Kitten is the new scaling engine — every noncreature cast recycles a Remora, an ETB, or a Sol Ring untap — though its mana-positive extension of the Hullbreaker loop is refuted (verified stack 005: mutually exclusive triggers, loop stays mana-neutral, one-time +1-float exit) and its remaining value line (the Remora reset) is still an unverified candidate. Structurally it is still a two-piece critical-mass deck (strategy:critical-mass) whose honest assembly rate is 40% by turn 6, so the pilot's real skill is the waiting game: draw-go control behind free countermagic and an uncounterable Supreme Verdict, threat deflection while the artifacts look harmless (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection), then one precisely-timed pivot — an assembled punisher board or the stack-002 Approach kill — taken inside the window where the table cannot profitably answer it (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). The cost of the rebuild is closing speed: wincon access dropped to 43% by t6, so protect the Approach line and get a Kitten payoff line verified.
